items.prompt:
When matter changes by heating or mixing in a sealed container, the total weight
A) always goes up
B) always goes down
C) stays the same
D) disappears

steps: Matter is conserved, so the sealed weight does not change.

items.prompt:
A 30 gram ice cube melts in a sealed bag. The water now weighs
A) 15 grams
B) 30 grams
C) 60 grams
D) 0 grams

steps: No matter left the sealed bag, so the weight is unchanged.

items.prompt:
Substance A (12 g) and substance B (8 g) are mixed in a closed jar. The total weight after is
A) 4 grams
B) 12 grams
C) 20 grams
D) 40 grams

steps: 12 plus 8 equals 20, and the closed jar traps all matter.

items.prompt:
Why do scientists use a closed container when a reaction makes a gas?
A) To make the gas heavier
B) So the gas cannot escape and all matter is weighed
C) To destroy the gas
D) To add matter
items.answer: B) So the gas cannot escape and all matter is weighed

steps: Trapping the gas keeps all the matter for weighing.

items.prompt:
A reaction in an OPEN cup makes the scale read lower afterward. The best explanation is
A) matter was destroyed
B) gas escaped into the air
C) weight is never conserved
D) the scale broke
items.answer: B) gas escaped into the air

steps: The gas carried matter out of the open cup.

items.prompt:
A student graphs weight-before vs weight-after for sealed changes. The points should show that
A) after is always larger
B) after is always smaller
C) before and after are equal
D) there is no pattern
items.answer: C) before and after are equal

steps: Conservation of weight means each pair matches.

items.prompt:
A log burns and the ash weighs far less than the log. The missing matter
A) was destroyed
B) left as gases and smoke into the air
C) turned into heat with no matter
D) became the scale
items.answer: B) left as gases and smoke into the air

steps: Burning releases gases and smoke; matter is not destroyed.

items.prompt:
Wet soil weighing 50 g is left in the sun in an open tray and later weighs 44 g. This is because
A) soil was destroyed
B) 6 g of water evaporated into the air
C) the soil gained weight
D) weight is not conserved
items.answer: B) 6 g of water evaporated into the air

steps: Water particles evaporated, carrying 6 grams of matter out of the open tray.
